---
title: '<span class="spondylolisthesis-module-title">Spondylolisthesis</span> <span class="spondylolisthesis-subsection-title">Introduction</span>'
pagetitle: "Spondylolisthesis – Introduction"
---

Spondylolisthesis is the forward slippage of one vertebra over the one directly below it, occurring most often at the lower lumbar levels. It is closely related to spondylolysis, a defect of the pars interarticularis; when such a defect is bilateral, the vertebra can slip forward, producing isthmic spondylolisthesis.

It is a common and clinically important cause of low back pain across all ages (reported prevalence approximately 4–6% in childhood and 5–10% in adults). In children and adolescents, it is a leading identifiable cause of back pain, especially in athletes who repeatedly hyperextend the spine; in older adults, the degenerative form contributes to back pain and lumbar spinal stenosis.

**Estimated time:** 45–60 minutes

::: {.learning-callout-body}

By the end of this module, you should be able to:

- [ ] Define spondylolisthesis and use key terminology correctly, including spondylolysis, pars interarticularis, anterolisthesis, retrolisthesis, and spondyloptosis
- [ ] Classify slips by etiology using the Wiltse-Newman classification and grade severity using Meyerding grades I–V
- [ ] Explain the mechanisms, natural history, and risk factors distinguishing isthmic from degenerative disease
- [ ] Recognize the clinical spectrum, from asymptomatic slips to back pain, radicular symptoms, and hamstring tightness
- [ ] Perform a focused history and examination and build an appropriate differential
- [ ] Select and interpret imaging and identify red flags warranting urgent referral
- [ ] Outline nonoperative and operative management, including pediatric and high-grade considerations

:::
